reason: A real Edit PDF attempt made the browser app unresponsive. The editor's existing-content path could perform unbounded paragraph reconstruction and quadratic fallback table-grid connectivity work on the browser main thread after worker inspection returned, then render one interactive React hitbox for every detected native object on the current page. Dense text/vector PDFs could therefore monopolize the UI both during inspection and when mounting the editable overlay.
affected_workflows: Edit PDF / open existing PDF for editing
Direct canvas selection and movement of existing PDF objects
notes: Bounds UI-thread paragraph reconstruction and fallback table-recovery pair work, preserves the full vector inspection for editing, adds a 30-second abortable native-inspection responsiveness budget that fails soft to overlay editing, and caps direct-canvas native hitboxes at 800 while prioritizing selected and semantic objects. Dense-page pointer-move snapping uses the same bounded hitbox set. The user's private PDF is not stored or committed; regression coverage uses synthetic in-memory inspection structures. Issue #31.
